chunks: 5686 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

“Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled concerning the blood money of a slain person that it is inherited by the heirs according to the Book of Allah, the Exalted, and according to their prescribed shares, if the slain person has no debt upon him, except that the maternal brothers and sisters do not inherit anything from his blood money.”

key_terms.الْوَرَثَةُ: the legal heirs of the deceased
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: an outstanding debt owed by the deceased
key_terms.دِيَةِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the blood money due for a person who was killed
key_terms.كِتَابِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: the divine basis for inheritance rules in the Quran

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the blood money of a murdered person in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the inheritance of the blood money of a murdered person. It states that the diyah is distributed among the heirs according to the shares set out in the Book of Allah, provided the deceased had no outstanding debt, while maternal siblings are excluded from inheriting from the diyah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5686 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"The Commander of the Faithful (as) ruled regarding the blood money (diyyah) of a murdered person that it is to be inherited by the heirs according to the Book of Allah (swt), the Exalted, and according to their prescribed shares, provided the murdered person has no outstanding debt. However, the maternal brothers and sisters do not inherit anything from the blood money."
